partners.mechanism_chain: WNT10B (HGNC:17609) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP472); WNT4 (HGNC:12817) —DISRUPTS→ WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP472); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP472) —LEADS_TO→ Split hand-foot malformation (HP:0001181); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP472) —LEADS_TO→ Mullerian aplasia (HP:0000001); WNT signaling pathway (WP:WP472) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperandrogenism (HP:0004749). Loss-of-function mutations in WNT10B and WNT4 disrupt the canonical WNT signaling pathway, leading to distinct but related developmental defects. In the context of split hand-foot malformation, WNT10B's role in limb bud patterning is impaired. In the context of mullerian aplasia and hyperandrogenism, WNT4's crucial function in female reproductive tract development and ovarian steroidogenesis is disrupted.
